source_refs.note: Book p. 284: 14.4.2 volume of the parallelepiped as (u x v).w, base area and height, the three cyclic forms, with its figure. Book errors: modulus bar missing in (i); 'be taking'. Teaching notes, Key points, mistakes are ours.

items.title: 14.4.2 The Volume of the Parallelepiped (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle page par humne scalar triple product ki definition parhi. Ab sawal yeh hai: is number ka matlab kya hai? Is page ka jawab bohat khoobsurat hai: \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w}\) us dabbe (parallelepiped) ka volume hai jo in teen vectors par banta hai. Yani ek algebraic hisaab seedha ek geometric cheez, hajm (volume), de deta hai. Chaliye dekhte hain kaise.

Kitab kehti hai: triple scalar product \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w}\) us parallelepiped ka volume hai jis ke conterminous edges \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) hon.

blocks.alt: A flat parallelepiped on three vectors u, v, w from the corner O. The base spanned by u and v is hatched and labelled Area of base = |u x v|. The vector u x v rises vertically from O; the angle theta lies between it and w. A dashed line from the tip of w meets the vertical at M with a right angle; a bar on the left marks height = |w| cos theta.
blocks.caption: Figure: parallelepiped with edges u, v, w; base area |u × v|, height |w| cos θ (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Parallelepiped kya hai? Isay "tirchha dabba" samajhiye: aisa thos (solid) jis ke chhe (6) chehre (faces) hon, har chehra parallelogram ho, aur aamne saamne ke chehre barabar aur parallel hon. Eent (brick) ya maachis ki dibiya is ki seedhi si misaal hai, jahan har chehra rectangle hai. Ab socho maachis ki dibiya ko upar se halka sa dhakka do to woh tirchhi ho jati hai; yahi parallelepiped hai.
Conterminous edges ka matlab hai woh kinare (edges) jo ek hi kone (corner) se shuru hon. Figure mein \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\) teeno kone \(O\) se nikalte hain. Dabbe ke baaqi nau (9) kinare inhi teen ki naqlen (copies) hain, is liye yeh teen vectors poora dabba tay kar dete hain.
Ab formula dekhiye. Dot product ki definition se:

blocks.text_alt: (u cross v) dot w equals modulus of u cross v times modulus of w times cos theta

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh koi naya formula nahin, yeh wahi dot product ki definition hai: \(\underline{a}\cdot \underline{b} = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\cos\theta\). Bas yahan \(\underline{a}\) ki jagah \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{b}\) ki jagah \(\underline{w}\) rakha gaya hai.
Dhyan dein: is liye \(\theta\) woh angle hai jo \(\underline{w}\) aur \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) ke darmiyan hai. \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) base par seedha khara (perpendicular) hai, jaise figure mein upar ki taraf jata hua teer. Yeh \(\underline{w}\) aur base ke darmiyan wala angle nahin; bohat se students yahin phisalte hain.
Is liye kitab do nateeje nikalti hai:

items: (i) \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) = us parallelogram ka area jis ki do saath wali (adjacent) sides \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab (i) mein "|u × v =" chhapti hai, yani modulus ki doosri lakeer (band karne wala \(|\)) ghaib hai. Sahi \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) hai: yeh base parallelogram ka area hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
(i) to aap 14.3 mein parh chuke hain: cross product ki lambai parallelogram ka area hoti hai. Ab (ii) ko samajhte hain: \(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) unchai kyun hai?
Unchai hamesha base se seedha upar naapi jati hai, yani \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) ki seedh mein. Figure mein \(\underline{w}\) ki nok se ek dashed line seedhi line par point \(M\) par 90 degree ka angle bana kar milti hai. Is tarah \(O\), \(M\) aur \(\underline{w}\) ki nok ek right-angled triangle banate hain jis ka right angle \(M\) par hai. Is triangle ka hypotenuse (sab se lambi side) \(|\underline{w}|\) hai aur \(O\) par angle \(\theta\) hai. Trigonometry ka purana rule: saath wali side = hypotenuse \(\times\cos\theta\). Is liye
\[OM = |\underline{w}|\cos\theta\]
Aur \(OM\) bilkul upar wale chehre ki base se unchai hai. Kyun: ek tirchhi seerhi (ladder) ki lambai us ki unchai nahin hoti; unchai zameen se seedha upar ka faasla hai. Yahan bhi \(|\underline{w}|\) seerhi ki lambai hai aur \(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) asal unchai.
Ab dono ko jor dein:

\[(\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w}\]
\[= |\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\,|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\]
\[= (\text{Area of parallelogram})(\text{height})\]
\[= \text{Volume of the parallelepiped}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh wahi purana rule hai jo aap ne choti classon mein parha: volume = base ka area \(\times\) unchai. Dabbe, cylinder, sab ke liye yahi. Scalar triple product ek hi waqt mein dono kaam kar deta hai: \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) base deta hai aur \(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) unchai. Is liye ek hi number mein poora volume aa jata hai.

Isi tarah agar \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) wale chehre ko base maan lein to
\[\text{Volume} = (\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\cdot \underline{u}\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "be taking the base plane" chhapti hai. Sahi lafz "by taking the base plane" hai, yani "base plane ko le kar".

Aur agar \(\underline{w}\) aur \(\underline{u}\) wale chehre ko base maan lein to
\[\text{Volume} = (\underline{w}\times \underline{u})\cdot \underline{v}\]
Is tarah humein yeh barabari milti hai:

blocks.text_alt: (u cross v) dot w equals (v cross w) dot u equals (w cross u) dot v

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is ka matlab saada hai: ek hi dabba teen mukhtalif chehron mein se kisi par bhi rakh dein, us ka volume nahin badalta. Isi liye teeno cyclic shaklen barabar hain. Yeh woh baat hai jo 14.4.1 mein humne kahi thi ke "saboot aage aayega"; lijiye, saboot aa gaya.
Ek aur faida: dot product commutative hai (\(\underline{a}\cdot \underline{b} = \underline{b}\cdot \underline{a}\)), is liye \((\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\cdot \underline{u} = \underline{u}\cdot(\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\). Pehli shakal se milayein to
\[(\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = \underline{u}\cdot(\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\]
yani dot aur cross apni jagah badal sakte hain, jawab wahi rehta hai. Example 23 yahi baat determinants se saabit karti hai.
Dhyan dein, sign ka masla: agar \(\underline{w}\) base ke doosri taraf ho (yani \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) ki ulti taraf), to \(\theta > 90^{\circ}\) hoga, \(\cos\theta\) negative, aur product negative aayega. Volume to negative nahin ho sakta, is liye us waqt product ki absolute value (sign hata kar) lete hain. Yeh baat kitab 14.4.3 ke Note mein kehti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek eent jaisa dabba lete hain (yeh hamara sawal hai): \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i}\), \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{j}\), \(\underline{w} = 4\underline{k}\). Yeh \(2\times 3\times 4\) ka seedha dabba hai, jis ka volume hum pehle se jaante hain: 24.
Ab formula se: \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v} = 2\underline{i}\times 3\underline{j} = 6(\underline{i}\times \underline{j}) = 6\underline{k}\).
Phir \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = 6\underline{k}\cdot 4\underline{k} = 24(\underline{k}\cdot \underline{k}) = 24\).
Bilkul wahi jawab! Is se yaqeen ho jata hai ke formula sach mein volume deta hai. Isi tarah side \(a\) wale cube ke liye \(a\underline{i}, a\underline{j}, a\underline{k}\) lein to jawab \(a^{3}\) aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar \(\underline{w}\) bhi \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) wale base plane mein hi parra ho to dabbe ka volume kya hoga? Socho, dabba bilkul pichak kar ek chapti sheet ban jayega.
Jawab: volume zero. Formula mein bhi yahi aata hai: tab \(\underline{w}\) base mein hai, to \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) par perpendicular hai, \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\). Yeh idea 14.4.5 (coplanar vectors) ki chaabi hai, yaad rakhiye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\) conterminous edges wale parallelepiped ka volume \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w}\) hai (positive number ke taur par).
2. \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) = base ka area; \(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) = unchai, jahan \(\theta\) = \(\underline{w}\) aur \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) ka angle.
3. \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = (\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\cdot \underline{u} = (\underline{w}\times \underline{u})\cdot \underline{v}\): dabba kisi bhi chehre par rakho, volume wahi.
4. Dot aur cross jagah badal sakte hain: \((\underline{u}\times \underline{v})\cdot \underline{w} = \underline{u}\cdot(\underline{v}\times \underline{w})\).
5. Product negative aaye to volume us ki absolute value hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\theta\) ko \(\underline{w}\) aur base ka angle samajh lena. Sahi: \(\underline{w}\) aur perpendicular \(\underline{u}\times \underline{v}\) ka angle.
2. \(|\underline{w}|\) ko hi unchai likh dena. Unchai \(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) hai; yeh \(|\underline{w}|\) ke barabar sirf tab hoti hai jab \(\underline{w}\) base par seedha khara ho.
3. Volume negative likh dena. Volume hamesha positive; minus aaye to hata dijiye.
4. Modulus ki lakeerein adhoori chhor dena (jaise kitab mein): \(|\underline{u}\times \underline{v}|\) dono taraf band kijiye.
